What the model knows, and what it guesses

  • The shape of the dent at a given depth was checked on presses the model never saw: at the centre down to 38 mm (1.2 mm RMS error over all 105 dots) and 30 mm left of it down to 32 mm. Other positions were never filmed; left and right are mirror images in the model.
  • How far a weight sinks rests on the stiffness, E = 178 kPa, fitted to dead weights of 1 to 2.4 kg on a pad over the whole top. Each weight alone gave 98 to 183 kPa, so read the sinks as ±40%.
  • Past about 4.6 kg the pressure under the base passes 12.5 kPa, the cells start to buckle and each extra kilogram sinks further. Nothing that heavy was filmed.
  • Over time, 12% of the stiffness relaxes with a 0.34 s time constant, so a weight keeps sinking for about a second, and a dent fades the same way after it is lifted. The weight's own bounce is left out: it presses with its full weight, ramped in over 0.15 s.
  • Colour is how far each point of the surface has moved. The black dots are the 105 dots painted on the filmed face.
